name: Bolivian Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of the andes of northwestern bolivia (la paz, cochabamba, and adjacent santa cruz)
description: Rotund, brown bird with long legs and a short tail restricted to the Bolivian Andes. Looks rather plain in the field, though may show a buffy tinge to the underparts.

name: Rusty-tinged Antpitta
rangeDescription: East slope of andes of northern peru (amazonas to eastern la libertad)
description: Medium-sized antpitta restricted to cloud forest along the east slope of the Andes in northern Peru. Adult is rich cinnamon brown with a white belly and throat (sometimes tinged yellow), a gray crown, and a bluish eye-ring.

name: Hainan Peacock-Pheasant
rangeDescription: Hainan (southern china)
description: Rare and often excruciatingly difficult to find, this is the only large gray game bird on Hainan. Usually detected by the loud, scratching noises made by flipping and scuffling leaves as it forages.

name: Fire-tufted Barbet
rangeDescription: Montane forest of malay peninsula and sumatra; recorded southern thailand
description: Beautiful emerald-green barbet. Note silvery cheeks, white forehead, and black chinstrap; namesake reddish tuft above the base of the bill is small and often difficult to see from a distance.

name: Kirtland's Warbler
rangeDescription: Jack-pine area of michigan; winters in bahamas
description: One of the largest and rarest warblers. Breeds only in young jack pine forests in northern Michigan and Wisconsin.

name: Palawan Crow
rangeDescription: Southern philippines (balabac, culion, mindoro, and palawan)
description: Large black crow endemic to the western Philippines, from Mindoro west to Palawan. Plumage has an iridescent dark blue sheen when seen up close.

name: Green Catbird
rangeDescription: Eastern australia (dawes range, queensland to jervis bay, new south wales)
description: Chunky rainforest bird with emerald green upperparts, dark eye, and green-olive underparts with pale streaking. Inhabits the east coast of Australia from southeastern Queensland to the south coast of New South Wales, thus does not overlap with Spotted Catbird.

name: Glossy Flowerpiercer
rangeDescription: Andes of colombia to western venezuela, ecuador and far northern peru
description: This glossy-black flowerpiercer has a distinctive silvery patch on the shoulder. Most similar to Black Flowerpiercer, which is smaller and lacks the shoulder patch in most of its range (although in east Andes in Colombia, Black Flowerpiercer has a small gray shoulder patch).

name: Western Fieldwren
rangeDescription: South of line from pt. culver to geraldton (except far southwestern corner, western australia)
description: Small bird of open arid shrubland and grasslands in southwestern Western Australia. Pale brown above, whitish below, with distinct pale supercilium, streaking on head chest, and long, cocked tail.

name: Gilded Hummingbird
rangeDescription: Bolivia to paraguay, uruguay, southeastern brazil, and northern argentina
description: Medium-sized hummingbird with a long, straight bill which is red with a black tip. Deceptively dull-looking, but in the right light has a golden-green back and breast and a bronze tail.

name: Finsch's Euphonia
rangeDescription: Southeastern venezuela to the guianas and northern brazil (northern roraima)
description: Small finch of forest canopy; often seen perched on bare branches. Males have yellow forecrown and belly contrasting with dark throat; females mostly dull yellow and green.

name: Blue-billed Teal
rangeDescription: Locally in sub-saharan africa and madagascar
description: Small brownish duck with a blue bill, dark cap, and a dark smudge on the pale tan cheek. In flight, look for white, black, and green stripes on the wing.

name: Yellow Bittern
rangeDescription: Southern asia, malay archipelago, new guinea region, and southern oceania
description: Very small heron of marshy, well-vegetated water bodies. Adult pale orangish brown or yellow, depending on the light, with a narrow dark cap.

name: Rufous-browed Conebill
rangeDescription: Mountains of northeastern colombia and far southwestern venezuela (táchira)
description: This small warblerlike bird is rich cinnamon below and gray above. The namesake rufous brow is fairly obvious but blends into the face.

name: Pied Shrike-Babbler
rangeDescription: Highlands of java
description: Stout medium-sized bird of foothill and montane forests. Endemic to Java, where it is the only “white-browed” shrike-babbler.

name: Basra Reed Warbler
rangeDescription: Southern iraq (tigris and euphrates valleys); winters kenya to malawi
description: Medium-sized Acrocephalus warbler with cold gray-olive-brown plumage and whitish underparts. Note the long and slender bill and the short eyebrow that reaches just behind the eye.

name: Socotra Sparrow
rangeDescription: Socotra islands (socotra, samha, and darsa)
description: Typical “rufous sparrow”, with a striped back and a gray crown, nape, and rump. Males have a black bib, and are brighter overall, with more rufous on the face and shoulder.

name: Band-tailed Antshrike
rangeDescription: Suriname, french guiana, and northeastern amazonian brazil
description: A rarely encountered large antshrike. Both sexes are distinctive; male is mostly black with a broad white tail band, whereas female is mostly rusty-colored with a black face and throat.

name: Black-legged Seriema
rangeDescription: Chaco of paraguay and adjacent bolivia to central argentina
description: Tall terrestrial predator of the Chaco region. Plumage distinctively shaggy.

name: Benguet Bush Warbler
rangeDescription: Mountains of northern luzon (northern philippines)
description: A fairly small, slender bird of lower montane grassy valleys. Warm brown above and on the belly, with a white throat and a faintly streaked grayish chest.
